title: io_uring Completion Queue Entry (CQE)
summary: An io_uring CQE is a 16-byte (or 32-byte with CQE32) structure written by the kernel into the completion queue ring. It carries the user_data from the SQE, the result (bytes transferred or negative errno), and flags (more completions pending, buffer id used).

ext.summary: An io_uring CQE is a 16-byte (or 32-byte with CQE32) structure written by the kernel into the completion queue ring. It carries the user_data from the SQE, the result (bytes transferred or negative errno), and flags (more completions pending, buffer id used).

structure.meaning: Echoed from the SQE; identifies which operation completed.
Result: bytes transferred on success, negative errno on failure (-EINVAL, -EAGAIN, ...).
IORING_CQE_F_BUFFER (buffer id in bits 16-31), IORING_CQE_F_MORE (more completions coming), IORING_CQE_F_SOCK_NONEMPTY.

ext.example_decoded: CQE: user_data=0, res=5 (5 bytes read), no flags
notes: CQEs are 16 bytes by default; IORING_SETUP_CQE32 makes them 32 bytes (extra 16 for big_cqe).
The CQ ring is single-producer (kernel) / single-consumer (application).
IORING_CQE_F_MORE indicates a multishot operation (e.g. multishot accept/recv) will produce more CQEs.
Buffer id (from IORING_CQE_F_BUFFER) tells which registered buffer was used for IOSQE_BUFFER_SELECT.
